text: Metra trains end their runs at four downtown terminals. To cross the region, you change trains.
A new tunnel links the lines, so trains run through downtown. This X1 runs from South Chicago to Highland Park.
59th St, where this ride begins, is the Metra stop closest to the Obama Presidential Center in Jackson Park.
From Hyde Park to 18th St, the X1 runs on the Metra Electric, as it runs today, stopping where its trains stop.
Just past 18th St, the X1 leaves the Metra Electric for a new tunnel under Roosevelt Rd and Clinton St.
This tunnel doesn't exist yet. The Clinton–Roosevelt Connector would run under Roosevelt Rd and Clinton St.
Riders from the South Side would reach the West Loop without changing trains.
Frequent, all-day trains on Metra's tracks: the missing middle between the ‘L’ and commuter rail.
Today, Metra trains here end their runs and turn back. With the tunnel, they could run through.
X1 to X4 would share this new tunnel; X5 and X6 would run through Union Station. All six would use mostly existing Metra tracks.
About 48,500 more workers could reach O'Hare within an hour by transit.

text: North of Chicago/Halsted, the X1 would join Metra's Union Pacific North tracks, as they run today.
Trains on the UP North keep to the left-hand track, a holdover from the Chicago & North Western, which built the line.
